next_question: After the runtime lane removes the first-20 locatableSample cap, does full DOM enumeration confirm that the a→link-inclusive page-type ordering changes between truncated and full-DOM, and does the null-model pairwise agreement exceed chance on full-DOM data?
why_next: This experiment partially resolves the parent's provenance mismatch (2/3 definitions verified, 1 invalid due to copy-paste bug) but the formal measurement remains blocked: (1) the estimator inflates bias 4-7x by conflating total DOM counts with locatable counts (audit V1); (2) the canonical analysis script is not committed; (3) the ISOLATED-A-LINK stored results are invalid. The blocking substrate fix (locatableSample cap removal in runtime lane) would provide true full DOM enumeration, resolving the estimator validity issue and enabling a reproducible measurement. Additionally, the canonical script must be committed with 3-definition per-role filtering and cart_1 deduplication before re-run.

established: The uncommitted 3-definition per-role-filtered analysis is reconstructable from frozen raw evidence for DEF-FULL-MAP and DEF-FORM-ONLY within ±0.001 density tolerance, identical orderings, and identical C3 per definition (reconstruction_complete.json, audit V2_recomputed_metrics per_definition_comparison)

ISOLATED-A-LINK in stored analysis_results.json is invalid: byte-identical to DEF-FULL-MAP for all 7 tasks (truncated_count 8 vs correct 2, full_count 454.1 vs 393-397, densities 0.00516 vs 0.00128). This is a copy-paste bug, not a valid a-only analysis (audit V3_isolated_copy_paste_invalid)

Committed analyze.py uses all-role density (a+button+form+input+combobox+div+label+span) producing FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (8 tasks, C3=false); stored results use per-definition filtering producing SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST (7 tasks, DEF-FULL-MAP C3=true). The algorithmic difference explains the different verdicts (report.md section 3-4)
Cart_1 deduplication: raw evidence has 8 valid measurements but only 7 unique task_ids; committed script includes both cart_1 entries (result.json deduplication)

Directional finding: first-20 document-order truncation introduces page-type-dependent ordering change, robust across both inflated-DOM and locatable-scaled estimators and across committed and stored analysis scripts (parent carry_forward established)
rejected: Hypothesis that the provenance gap is irreconcilable — REJECTED: 2/3 definitions reconstruct perfectly from raw evidence (null_control outcome: 0/3 matches did not occur)
Hypothesis that stored ISOLATED-A-LINK results are valid — REJECTED: byte-identical to DEF-FULL-MAP, cannot be reproduced by a-only filtering (audit V3)
Hypothesis that committed analyze.py is the canonical 3-definition analysis — REJECTED: committed script uses different algorithm (all-role density) than the 3-definition per-role-filtered approach
unknown: Whether full DOM enumeration (locatableSample cap removal) changes density magnitudes, ordering significance, and null distribution shape beyond the tag-count estimator — the estimator inflates bias 4-7x (audit V1); true full enumeration needed via runtime substrate fix

Whether committed analyze.py should be accepted as canonical (all-role density, 8 tasks) or a new script with 3-definition filtering and deduplication should be committed — until committed, measurement remains non-reproducible from HEAD (audit required_fixes)

Whether corrected ISOLATED-A-LINK (ordering_changed=False) would alter C3 conclusions — recomputed ordering is cart>detail>product_listing identical to full ordering, failing C1 (result.json observations)

Whether the product_listing vs detail ordering swap is statistically significant — means within 2% inflated or 0.016 vs 0.008 locatable-scaled, n=3 per type, n=1 distinct cart, no CI reported (audit V4_small_N_single_site)
Whether menuitem/tab contribute additively when present — 0 counts in this sample, requires sample where those roles appear (parent carry_forward unknown)
do_not_assume: Do not assume ISOLATED-A-LINK stored verdict (ordering_changed=True) is valid — it is based on copy-paste data identical to DEF-FULL-MAP; correct computed verdict is ordering_changed=False (audit V3)

Do not assume the 98% relative bias is a valid locatable-density point estimate — it conflates total DOM counts (393-397 links) with locatable counts (~19 links); proper bound is 14-69% depending on page type (audit V1)

Do not assume the FALSIFIED verdict from EXP-INTEL-35112013458 is fully explained by truncation — this experiment estimates ordering change but does not re-run the null ROLE_MAP test on full estimates

Do not assume C3 passes universally — it passes for DEF-FULL-MAP only; DEF-FORM-ONLY fails for all 7 tasks (random samples show higher bias than truncation for form-heavy definitions) (parent carry_forward do_not_assume)
Do not assume ordering differences between product_listing and detail are statistically significant — means within 2% with n=3 per type and n=1 cart, no CI reported (audit V4)
Do not assume results generalize to other sites — bounded to n=7 distinct tasks, 1 Magento site, truncated-first-20 vs tag-count-estimated full DOM (audit V4, parent carry_forward)

Do not assume the random baseline advantage (1% mean for DEF-FULL-MAP) is scientifically meaningful — within simulation noise (1000 draws, fixed seed) and definition-dependent (parent carry_forward do_not_assume)
